verdict: At the top 20% of road length, the model (road features only, no death history) captured 66% of later deaths versus 52% for the best past-deaths baseline (past deaths on the same road): +21 points, 95% interval +3 to +38. At the top 10% it was 55% versus 45%: +10 points, interval −7 to +28 (a tie). The model combined with past deaths on the same road did best at the top 10%: 55%, +10 points, interval −3 to +24. The test set is small (29 deaths), so treat these as estimates.
features: distance to a bus stop (less risk)
second_region: San Bernardino, CA: trained on 2019–2021, tested on 2022–2023 (127 deaths). Road features only captured 78% of later deaths in the top 20% of road length vs 58% for the best past-deaths baseline (+24 points, 95% interval +16 to +33); at the top 10%: 54% vs 52% (+2, interval −6 to +12).
